Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFæ OF THE FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT -42. s 12 June 2008 At-n. ALEJANDRO R. ABESAMIS Provincial Administrator and Concurrent Provincial Legal Officer — OIC Provincial Capitol Building Palayan City Dear Atty. Abesamis: This has reference to your letter seeking our legal opinion on the following issues involving the confirmation of your appointment as Provincial Administrator of Nueva Ecija by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan thereof, viz: A. B. ' 'Whether the Sangguniang Panlalazvigan may deny the confirmation of my appointment based on ground which is not any of the qualifications for Provincial Administrator enumerated in Section 480, Article IO of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991; and Whether the Sangguniang Panlalazvigan which has otherwise found me as possessing all the qualifications but nevertheless denied my confirmation on ground not specified in the law may legally be deemed to have confirnzed my appointment just the same.' Among others, you represented that all the Sangguniang Panlalawigan members during its deliberation on the confirmation of your appointment as Provincial Administrator signified either directly or indirectly that you have all the qualifications as provided for in Section 480 of the Local Government Code. However, despite thereof, the Sanggunian did not confirm your appointment by a vote of 4-6 with one member abstaining. Apparently, based on the attached excerpt of the aforesaid deliberation the six (6) Sangguniang Panlalawigan members voted "no" to your confirmation as Provincial Administrator because they were of the belief that either you cannot be an effective Provincial Administrator for you failed to recommend and/or advise the Vice Governor, who was then the Acting Governor when the Governor of Nueva Ecija was on leave of absence, on matters relative to the management and administration of Nueva Ecija when you were still the Provincial Administrator, and on the

-2- anticipation of diversity between the executive and the legislative branches in the Province of Nueva Ecija should you be again the Provincial Administrator. Both apprehensions based on the Memorandum you issued then as the Provincial Administrator advising the employees of the provincial government of your securing legal opinion from this Department on the legality of the series of Memoranda issued by Vice-Governor Edward Thomas Joson in his capacity as Acting Governor. Said Memoranda directed certain officials and employees to assume and perform the functions of certain offices effectively replacing the officials appointed by Governor Umali. The aforesaid DILG's legal opinion did not favor Acting Governor Joson's aforementioned acts. Indeed, based thereon, you issued another Memorandum saying that the "acts committed by concerned officials by virtue under the authority of illegal memorandum despite knowledge of the DILG opinion shall be deemed in bad faith and be severely dealt with". This latter Memorandum allegedly caused the non-confirmation of your appointment by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. May we invite your attention to Section 463 (d) of the LGC of 1991, which provides that: "Section 463. Officials of the Provincial Government (d) Unless otherwise provided herein, heads of deparbnents and offices shall be appointed by the governor with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang panlalazvigan members, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. The sangguniang panlalazvigan shall act on the appointment within fifteen (15) days from the date of its submission; otherwise the same shall be deemed confirmed; On the other hand, Section 480 (a) of the LGC provides, thus: -3- "Section 480. Qualifications, Term, Power and Duties. — (a) No person shall be appointed administrator unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, holder of a college degree preferably in public administration, law, or any other related course from a recognized college or university, and a first grade civil service eligible or its equivalent. He must have acquired experience in management and administration work for at least five (5) years in the case of the provincial or city administrator, and three (3) years in the case of the municipal administrator." Corollary to the foregoing, Section 1 (e), Rule V of Civil Service Commission Memorandum Circular No. 40, s 1998, provides that "appointment in local government units for submission to the Commission shall be accompanied, in addition to the common requirements, by the following: xxx (ii) Certification by the Municipal/City/ProvinciaI Accountant/Budget Officer

-3- that funds are available (iii) For appointment to department head, Sanggunian Resolution embodying the concurrence of the majority of its members as provided for under Section 443 (d), RA 7160; provided that if said appointment is not concurred in by the Sanggunian within fifteen (15) days, certification to that effect by the HRMO shall be issued in lieu of the required Resolution". Noticeably, as to the required concurrence of appointment by sanggunian, Section I (e) of the aforequoted Memorandum Circular mentions only Section 443 (d) of RA 7160; said Section refers only to Municipality. This might lead us to a conclusion then that only Sangguniang Bayans are required to concur appointments made by their However, paragraph (ii) thereof Mayors as their appointing authority. mentions Certification by the Provincial Accountant/Budget Officer as one of the additional requirements for the submission of an appointment to the CSC. Ergo, and pursuant to Section 463 of the LGC, it is our view that appointment in Provincial governments also requires Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution embodying the concurrence of the majority of their Sanggunian members for submission to the CSC. Coming now to your first query, we answer in the negative. If the appointee possesses all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications as mandated by pertinent laws, the Sanggunian has no discretion to deny the statutorily required concurrence since if that would be allowed, we are of the view that the Sanggunian will already be encroaching into the appointing prerogative of the Governor and in effect is already substituting the Governor's appointing discretion in the process. It bears stressing that the Governor, as the appointing authority, exercises and enjoys wide latitude of discretion as to who shall be appointed to a particular position. On the other hand, the power given to the Sanggunian to concur such appointment of the Governor is to be construed as merely an act of confirming that the appointee possesses all the minimum qualifications set by law for the position and that he has none of the disqualification under the LGC or other existing laws. Verily, such requirement of concurrence cannot be made to extend to the act of confirming the exercise of appointing discretion by the appointing authority. At this juncture, we would like to remind you that abuse of authority by local elective officials is not sanctioned by law and is not without remedy under our justice system. As to your second query, may we invite your attention to the aforequoted CSC MC No. 40, s 1998 particularly the provision on the fifteen (15) days period within which the Sanggunian is required to act on appointments. If the Sanggunian Panlalawigan of Nueva Ecija acted on your appointment outside of the 15-day period (for it cannot be inferred from your letter or even from the attached excerpt of such deliberation as to when the deliberation by the Sanggunian of your appointment happened), the statutory presumption pursuant to CSC MC No. 40 s 1998 shall work to your favor. Your appointment shall be deemed confirmed and can be properly submitted to the CSC for attestation notwithstanding aforesaid deliberation by the Sanggunian provided the HRMO should first issue a certification that the Sanggunian Panlalawigan failed to act within 15 days from submission of the appointment. This is the only case

-4- wherein your appointment is deemed confirmed even without the Sanggunian's resolution embodying their concurrence. Be that as it may, may we note that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan has already issued Kapasiyahan Big. 126, series of 2008 wherein said body did not confirm your appointment as Provincial Administrator. Hence, if you are nonetheless determined to question the substantive validity of the subject Resolution using as grounds our discussion above, you may file an action for Declaratory Relief in accordance with Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court. Please be informed that this Department is bereft of any authority to declare invalid any measure, such as a Resolution, passed by the local sanggunians. Only courts can make such declaration. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUST EA. PANADER U ndersecretary irector Josefina Castilla-GO DILG Regional Office No. 03 San Femando City, Pampanga
